study.question: Does reversing auxiliary outcome deviations while retaining their mean-target error contribution change the external-sign effect on click validation AUC? Observed full/native source favors reversed sign: g3-r0067 true-label negative/positive=0.6689610675617089/0.6683760511656333. Mean-only g3-r0068 bridges are nearly sign-neutral at 0.6686874913267814/0.6686740458787336. Label-deviation-only g3-r0068 instead favors positive: 0.6683408024435132/0.6687193398498718. These are controlled single-seed observations, not independent repeated support. Removing M as in r0068 changes source geometry and cannot establish that D is harmful when combined with M.
study.hypothesis: At a fixed graph let G be true-label auxiliary cotangents, M mean-target cotangents and D=G-M. The interaction of the mean-target and label-deviation components before nonlinear Q/pivot extraction helps determine the useful sign. Reflecting D in its original mixture, G_ref=M-D=2M-G, may attenuate or reverse the native negative-versus-positive AUC gap. This is a provisional explanation. It does not predict additive AUC effects, nor does a D-only sign reversal logically imply a reflected-mixture reversal.

study.proposed_difference: Change only the source_loss coefficient map and its constructor/config choice. Full source uses L_true+0*L_mean; reflection uses -L_true+2*L_mean. Both BCE graphs execute in every arm. The implied target 2*ybar-y may be outside[0,1], so it is never passed to BCE; the finite scalar linear combination is differentiated only to source collection edges. Detached cotangents enter an exact-zero surrogate, so the scalar reported loss and private gradients remain true joint BCE. The resulting source only selects the batch-global bit of the inherited canonical fixed-angle transfer. Four standalone modules form source{full,reflected} x external sign{negative,positive}. No new parameters, RNG, persistent statistics or inputs. No claim of originality: authorized gradient-literature search returned no hits, so broader priority remains unverified. Before any full training unit, the host must use its authorized preflight to check fresh train forward/loss/backward and eval (including odd validation remainder), finite true BCE and gradients, no label access in forward, train-only cache release, exact forward/state parity at common initialization across arms, identical true private gradients, unchanged parameter counts, native transfer support/radius, and empty/singleton/constant-label/zero-source cases. Verify at a fixed state g_reflected approximately equals 2*g_mean-g_true, source bits differ when the intervention is active, and native full-source routing agrees with the old native-bit path. Existing source_bit_diagnostics is an optional detached fixed-state probe, not an automatically collected API; all prior receipts say candidate_diagnostics=not_requested. No new diagnostic endpoint is assumed. If the host cannot supply these probes, report them as unavailable and limit any mechanism interpretation to validation contrasts; never invent bit rates or checks. All preflight and failures consume budget.
predictions: At fixed state before numerical cast, reflected source equals 2M-G and retains the mean-target term while negating D. Forward predictions, private gradients and native transfer geometry match across cells at that state.
Full-source bridges reproduce same-sign g3-r0067 true-label AUC within1e-6, with unchanged capacity. Failure blocks source attribution until execution/numerical differences are resolved.

Primary prospective interaction I=(AUC_full_negative-AUC_full_positive)-(AUC_reflected_negative-AUC_reflected_positive) is expected positive under the attenuation hypothesis. Native historical gap is0.0005850163960756; record both simple effects and I, without selecting only the better reflected sign.
If the reflected mixture instead preserves or enlarges the native gap despite active bit disagreement and verified parity, the D-only sign pattern does not support the proposed mixture explanation.

All-task AUC/Logloss, full-population click Logloss, history slices with counts, parameter counts, wall/train time, memory and model inference throughput/latency remain secondary. Empty-history differences can arise indirectly via shared parameters; they are not direct transfer evidence. Complete train-plus-validation units remain near450-480s/arm (recent training alone412-420s) and inference work should be unchanged, subject to measurement.
falsifiers: After successful full-source bridges and active fixed-state bit disagreement, no attenuation/reversal (I<=0) contradicts this directional mixture hypothesis for the frozen seed; a small positive I alone is inconclusive without independent paired repetitions.
Equal full/reflected bits or widespread source/tangent degeneracy makes the intervention ineffective; a null AUC then cannot refute useful outcome deviations.

Changed forward output/state, private gradients, parameter capacity, input availability or native radius/support invalidates attribution. Bridge AUC error>1e-6 requires a discriminating numerical follow-up, not a mechanism conclusion.

No reproducible advantage over click-only remains a falsifier for useful auxiliary supervision at the task level. Any apparent gain here is validation-selected and preliminary until supported by admissible paired repetitions and a separately frozen closed assessment.
alternative_explanations: All outcomes so far use one fixed seed and one repeatedly queried validation day; deterministic bridge replay is numerical reproducibility, not an independent replication or mechanism contrast.
Only a discontinuous batch-global sign is replaced. Reflection can leave that sign unchanged; without measured fixed-state disagreement a null contrast is not informative about label utility.
Native true-label radius/support and private heads retain label information; this does not test removal of all auxiliary information. Subsequent learned states and optimizer trajectories diverge.

BCE cancellation, bf16 collection/scatter, repeated feature IDs and nonlinear pivot selection can alter small source residuals. Row-space orthogonality does not imply parameter-space or optimizer-step orthogonality.

Reflection preserves mean and squared deviations but not binary label support, label histogram, or full cotangent norm. This is a signed-deviation intervention, not random-label independence or an equal-source-norm test.

Trajectory review: joint versus click-only gain0.0006024 and blocked==click-only support a shared-context pathway locally; rolled-label harm does not prove a unique mechanism. Product-only outperforms residual-only; r0041 FP32/FP64 collected gradients changed outcomes, making arithmetic controls essential. Paired source permutations in r0064 reproduce native AUC exactly; occupied-cycle r0065 improves only0.000000203, so that incumbent difference is not scientifically meaningful. r0066 label cycle and r0067 mean-only underperform the native negative cell, while r0068 D-only reverses sign and its mean bridges replay exactly. These positive/null/unsuccessful trajectories motivate mixture attribution rather than declaring the latest branch a mechanism success. No failed execution is listed in the supplied trajectory index; previous_runtime_error is null. Older unavailable campaigns are not local evidence.
